question: In a stab wound, the depth of the wound track is greater than the length of the surface wound; in an incised wound, the surface length exceeds the depth.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is TRUE. The stab-vs-incised rule is: stab wound has DEPTH greater than surface LENGTH (weapon penetrated inward); incised wound has LENGTH greater than DEPTH (weapon was drawn along the surface). This relationship is fundamental to weapon type inference in medicolegal reporting.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. This dimensional relationship is the defining distinguishing criterion: stab wound (depth > length — produced by a pointed weapon penetrating inward) versus incised wound (length > depth — produced by a sharp-edged weapon drawn across the surface). This distinction has direct medicolegal implications for weapon reconstruction.
